A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Satori and contain readable methods, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–E. Existing content can be matched reliably across layout changes and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original Satori benchmark evaluations, self-correction and scaling analyses, and component ablations, including the reflection-bonus experiment in Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds experiments removing RAE and the ORM preference bonus in Appendix E, Tables 7–8.

M1.justification: The proposed COAT actions, format tuning, PPO training, RAE algorithm, reward components, and iterative self-improvement procedure are unchanged. The new component-removal experiments evaluate ablated variants without revising the proposed method.

E1.justification: Training sources and mathematical and out-of-domain evaluation coverage remain unchanged. The new ablations use the existing GSM8K, MATH500, OlympiadBench, AMC2023, and AIME2024 benchmarks.

E2.justification: Tables 7–8 add two ablated comparators against full Satori: 'No RAE' and 'Only Rule-based.' The latter retains the reflection bonus according to its accompanying text. Existing external-model comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The new experiments introduce controls that remove RAE during RL training or remove the ORM while retaining rule-based and reflection rewards. Existing dataset splits, model sizes, training settings, and zero-shot greedy pass@1 evaluation remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices E.2–E.3 add focused tests of the contributions of RAE and the ORM preference bonus. Existing ablations and analyses are retained; the offline-versus-online restart-buffer discussion moves from E.2 to E.4 without substantive revision.

E5.justification: Existing graphical bands and error bars in Figures 3–4 remain unchanged. Tables 7–8 add point accuracies without introducing repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Existing results in Tables 1–6 are unchanged. Table 7 newly reports MATH500/AMC2023 scores of 81.6/57.5 without RAE, versus 85.6/67.5 with RAE; Table 8 reports 82.8/62.5 without ORM versus the same full-model scores. GSM8K slightly favors both ablations, and AIME2024 ties with and without RAE. These are additional configuration-specific results, not revised full-model performance.

T1.justification: Mathematical definitions, objectives, and reward formulas are unchanged. Section 4.2 adds an intuitive connection between state coverage and policy bounds, citing prior work, but explicitly leaves rigorous theoretical justification to future work; it supplies no new formal result or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same scientific contributions: autoregressive search within one LLM, small-scale format tuning followed by RL, strong mathematical reasoning, and out-of-domain transfer. The added ablations support existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 adds a state-coverage rationale for RAE and acknowledges the absence of rigorous theoretical justification. Appendix E newly interprets the ablations as supporting RAE and hybrid rewards, although the tables show exceptions to a uniform performance-degradation interpretation. The existing online-buffer limitation is retained.

D1.justification: The abstract changes the stated availability of code, data, and models from a future release to being fully open-sourced, using the same project link. Appendix D's implementation details, hyperparameters, data processing, and training recipes are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Kakade and Langford (2002), connecting RAE's broader initial-state coverage to prior reinforcement-learning insights. The remaining related-work discussion and positioning relative to other reasoning methods are unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds a short RAE explanation, two appendix subsections, acknowledgments, and a generic impact statement, and updates publication and release-status text. Most existing prose and the overall section structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds compact Tables 7–8, introduces running headers, removes the title icon, and rearranges some figures and text, including moving Figure 3 to page 8. Existing figures and tables otherwise retain their displays; the final buffer discussion extends onto page 38.

improvement.justification: Tables 7–8 strengthen the empirical support for existing design choices by directly testing removal of RAE and the ORM preference bonus. The added rationale and explicit deferral of rigorous theory also clarify the argument. These are limited gains: headline results remain unchanged, the new comparisons lack uncertainty reporting, and their broad interpretation does not fully acknowledge benchmark-specific exceptions.
